Hi Aisha — thanks for the detail and for the usage file. High level: yes, we can model a two-tier packaging approach and map premium runtime features to just the Priority endpoints.

Quick summary for procurement:
- "Core" plan = base per-token rate + shared KV cache and standard batching.
- "Priority" overlay = additional per-token premium for endpoints pinned to the Priority routing policy; Priority can also carry feature toggles (persistent KV, higher burst concurrency).
- Billing options: we can invoice as blended usage (single invoice with line items) or two separate SKUs if your accounting needs separation.

Two clarifying questions before I send a recommended quote:
1) Do you want Priority capacity to be a % of total tokens per day (e.g., top 10% of traffic) or a fixed reserved slot (e.g., 2 dedicated GPUs)?
2) Are you expecting to switch deployment mode mid-quarter or migrate permanently (Dedicated -> Hosted)? Proration differs slightly in each case.

Looping Marissa (Customer Success) for rollout impact and Rishi (Solutions) for the tech mapping — will follow up with a short proposal and an example invoice.

Thanks all — technical recommendation below.

1) Start with %-based Priority (top 10%). Reason: minimal ops friction, immediate cost savings, no capacity reservation lead time. We can pin a consistent routing policy so that the top N% of requests get the Priority profile.

2) Feature mapping: persist KV on Priority only (saves memory across Core). Batching thresholds: Core = dynamic small batches, Priority = fixed larger batch size with pre-warmed kernels. That yields ~18-22% cost improvement vs enabling Priority features across all traffic.

3) Billing approach: propose dual-SKU for clarity to Procurement (Core SKU + Priority SKU). Offer a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of the estimated Priority spend in the first billing month if they commit to a 6-month pilot. If they truly need single blended invoice, we can provide it but the accounting team tends to prefer SKU separation.

4) Migration proration: switching deployment modes mid-quarter = pro-rated credit for unused reserved capacity (if moving from Dedicated) + one-time setup fee waiver for the first cutover in pilot. Exact numbers in the attached spreadsheet after Ben confirms Priority sizing.

Next steps: Ben, if you can confirm whether Synthetica prefers % or reserved, I'll run a cost model and drop the detailed numbers into the shared Drive link. Aisha/Procurement — would you be available for a 30m call next week (Aug 18-20)?

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
